c.tagline: Where East meets West amid minarets, cafes and mountains.

taxi.fareNote: Flag fall around 2.5 KM plus roughly 1 KM per km; always confirm the meter is running or agree a price beforehand.

emergency.note: Fire brigade: 123. General EU-style emergency 112 also works.

avoid.reason: Very safe in town; uncleared landmines remain in some rural areas — stay on marked paths/roads

hood_desc: The historic Ottoman-era old town of cobblestone lanes, copper workshops, mosques and cafes; best for first-time visitors who want to be steps from every major sight and nightlife.
The modern civic and business heart with government buildings, the Holiday Hotel, shopping and the National Museum; suits business travelers and those wanting easy tram access.
The main pedestrian shopping street (Ferhadija) linking old and new town, lined with cafes, boutiques and Austro-Hungarian architecture; good for travelers who want a central, walkable base.
A steep, atmospheric hillside quarter inside the old city walls with the Yellow Fortress and sweeping views; suits travelers wanting a quiet, authentic residential feel with fewer crowds.
A leafy spa town at the city's edge near the airport and Vrelo Bosne park; suits those seeking a relaxed, green base with thermal spas, away from the downtown bustle.

water.note: Fed by mountain springs and considered safe, though many visitors opt for bottled water as extra precaution.

transit.pay: Buy paper tickets from kiosks (cheaper) or pay the driver in cash for a slightly higher fare; validate tickets on board. A rechargeable BUS PLUS card is also available for frequent riders.
transit.hours: Trams and buses run roughly 05:00-23:00; limited night bus coverage after that, so taxis are the main late-night option.
transit.note: The Sarajevo tram, running since 1885, is one of the oldest urban tram systems in Europe.

train: Sarajevo Main Railway Station (services to Zagreb, Budapest via Mostar/Ploče lines vary)

tip.r: Rounding up the bill or leaving 10% at restaurants is appreciated but not obligatory.
